problem_statement: Zephyr lacks a generic GPIO controller for an external latch-backed, memory-mapped output port (e.g. a 74HC574 latched onto an FMC bank). Such a device should be usable through the standard GPIO API as an output-only controller with 8/16/32-bit register width and a configurable number of valid lines (ngpios). Because the latch may be write-only with no hardware readback, the driver must keep a software shadow of the last output value and expose it through readback. It must support masked writes that touch only the requested bits, set/clear/toggle of bits, configuration of a pin as output with an initial high or low level that updates the shadow, an initial-output value written to the latch at init, and rejection of unsupported configurations (input, pull-up/pull-down, open-drain, single-ended). Invalid pins and flag combinations must return errors.

verification.reason: The original statement is mostly complete, but it omits the required public interface names and an exact error code needed by the tests. These can be added without revealing the implementation.

problems.detail: The devicetree compatible string "gpio-mmio-latch" and the Kconfig option CONFIG_GPIO_MMIO_LATCH are required by the tests but are not given in the statement.
The tests require unsupported flag combinations to return the exact error -ENOTSUP, while the statement only says unsupported configurations must be rejected.

The tests check that readback returns the software shadow even when the backing register is changed independently, and that output operations update the backing register; this observable behavior should be stated explicitly.

problem_statement_fixed: Zephyr lacks a generic GPIO controller for an external latch-backed, memory-mapped output port (e.g. a 74HC574 latched onto an FMC bank). Such a device should be usable through the standard GPIO API as an output-only controller with 8/16/32-bit register width and a configurable number of valid lines (ngpios). Because the latch may be write-only with no hardware readback, the driver must keep a software shadow of the last output value and expose it through readback. It must support masked writes that touch only the requested bits, set/clear/toggle of bits, configuration of a pin as output with an initial high or low level that updates the shadow, an initial-output value written to the latch at init, and rejection of unsupported configurations (input, pull-up/pull-down, open-drain, single-ended). Invalid pins and flag combinations must return errors. The new driver must be enabled by the Kconfig option CONFIG_GPIO_MMIO_LATCH and selected by the device-tree compatible string "gpio-mmio-latch". Its binding must expose the latch register address (reg), the valid line count (ngpios), and the initial-output property whose value is written to the latch and recorded as the initial software shadow at init. Unsupported configurations must return -ENOTSUP.
